verdict.rationale: The product is a public GitHub repository whose source files are readable: prompts in prompts/, firmware config in hardware/hid_bridge/nimble_cfg.h, a flash.sh build script and a board_test.py tool, and users build and sign the app themselves. No evidence names the license, so the 'open license' half of the story is unproven. Missing for 10: an explicit open-source license (e.g., a LICENSE file or SPDX identifier), and independent confirmation of the license terms.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: The prompts are plain text in prompts/ and bundled with the app: edit them, rebuild, done.
Always build with flash.sh: it applies the BLE buffer sizes in hardware/hid_bridge/nimble_cfg.h.
Debugging without the phone app: hardware/tools/board_test.py plays the app over BLE from a Mac
A free Apple ID can sign it (re-sign every 7 days).
